da-overclaim.evidence: braid-action-tensor.md:5-10 states the homomorphism ρ_n: B_n → Aut(V^⊗n) 'For each object V ... and each n ≥ 2'. The Lean sibling only constructs/verifies the B₃ case: yang_baxter_braiding and BraidRepB3 act on (V⊗V)⊗V (braid-action-tensor.lean:174-231); there is no n-general ρ_n or far-commutativity formalisation.
da-overclaim.notes: The proposition claims the full B_n family; the formalisation establishes the single defining relation for B₃ (the generating braid relation) and packages it as braid_action_tensor : BraidRepB3. The .md 'Mathematical Novelty' note (l.31) accurately scopes the contribution as the B₃ Yang–Baxter chase, so the gap is between the proposition statement (all n) and what is proved (n=3 relation). Standard mathematically; minor overclaim of formalised scope.

da-referee-verdict.evidence: Proposition claims ρ_n: B_n→Aut(V^⊗n) for all n≥2 (braid-action-tensor.md:5-10); Lean establishes the generating relation for B₃ only (braid-action-tensor.lean:174-231) and omits far-commutativity.
da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: accept-with-minor-revision. referee_argument: This is the strongest block of the five — a correct, sorry-free categorical proof of the B₃ Yang–Baxter relation with honest novelty framing. The only objection is the scope mismatch: the proposition is stated for all n≥2 with the full Artin presentation (proof block invokes far-commutativity), while the Lean proves the single adjacent braid relation on (V⊗V)⊗V and never formalises the |i-j|≥2 commutation or the general-n homomorphism. Recommend either narrowing the proposition's formalised claim to B₃ or adding the far-commutativity lemma; mathematically the general result is standard so no falsity risk.
